title: rorca-wave-execution-fix
_notes: Bug fix spec. Three issues: (1) sub-worktree story results silently fail to persist to DB when HTTP POST to backend fails, causing 0/N stories passed with no diagnostic info. (2) users manually choose parallelism mode — backend should auto-select based on dependency graph analysis. (3) execution-engine.ts writes Claude stdout to log file but does NOT forward it to its own stdout — backend SSE buffer gets nothing, terminal is permanently blank for all runs using the new engine. This is a regression introduced when execution-engine.ts replaced run-loop.ts (first visible after rorca-opencode-integration completed). Sonnet-tier — targeted fixes, no new features.
_relatesTo: rorca-opencode-integration (wave execution was built here), rorca-e2e-testing (would catch these regressions). Standalone — no dependencies on pending specs.
_executionOrder: Run immediately — this is a bug fix for an existing feature. Run before rorca-context-intent-engine.

userStories.title: Fix Sub-Worktree Story Result Persistence
userStories.description: Sub-worktree story results are lost when the HTTP POST to the backend at :3030 fails silently. The Claude subprocess in a sub-worktree calls fetch() to POST story_started, story_passed, story_failed WAL events and story_results to the running backend. If this fetch fails (network hiccup, backend restart, port mismatch), the result is never recorded — story_results table gets zero rows for the run, WAL has only spec_approved, and the UI shows 0/N passed with no explanation. Fix: in execution-engine.ts and run-loop.ts, wrap all backend POST calls (emitWalEvent, markStoryPassed, gitCommitStory, the POST to /api/pipeline/story-result) in a retry wrapper with 3 attempts and 1s backoff. If all retries fail, write the result to a local fallback file at `<worktree>/.rorca-result.json` containing { storyId, status, runId, retries, elapsed }. The pipeline trigger process (pipeline.ts) polls for `.rorca-result.json` files in active sub-worktrees every 5 seconds and syncs any unprocessed results to the DB. This ensures results are never silently dropped.
acceptanceCriteria: emitWalEvent() retries POST 3 times with 1s backoff before failing
On all-retry failure, result is written to <worktree>/.rorca-result.json with { storyId, status, runId, retries, elapsed, ts }
pipeline.ts polls active sub-worktrees for .rorca-result.json every 5 seconds and syncs unprocessed results
story_results table always has a row for every story that ran, even if POST failed mid-run
WAL events story_started, story_passed, story_failed are always recorded (via retry or fallback file sync)
Fallback file is deleted after successful sync to DB
A simulated POST failure (kill backend mid-run) results in results being recovered via fallback file when backend restarts

userStories.title: Auto-Select Execution Mode from Dependency Graph
userStories.description: Users currently choose wave parallel execution manually (parallelism toggle in the pipeline trigger UI). This leads to bad outcomes: running a 6-story spec with a single-story Wave 0 (like rorca-forge-brief-first) with parallelism=3 provides zero benefit and introduces sub-worktree overhead. The backend should auto-select sequential vs wave based on the dependency graph. Logic to add to pipeline.ts trigger handler, BEFORE spawning the execution engine: (1) Compile the dependsOn DAG into wave groups (topological sort — same algorithm already used in wave execution). (2) Calculate effective parallelism: max(stories per wave across all waves). (3) Decision rule: if effective_parallelism < 2 OR total_stories < 5 OR all waves have exactly 1 story → use sequential. Otherwise use wave parallel. (4) Log the decision: '[orchestration] Using sequential (max wave size: 1, stories: 6)' or '[orchestration] Using wave parallel (max wave size: 3, stories: 18)'. Remove the parallelism toggle from the pipeline trigger UI entirely — replace with a read-only badge showing the auto-selected mode and the wave structure (e.g. 'Sequential · 6 stories' or 'Wave parallel · 4 waves · max 3 parallel').
acceptanceCriteria: Pipeline trigger auto-selects sequential when max wave size is 1 (all stories form a linear chain)
Pipeline trigger auto-selects sequential when total story count < 5
Pipeline trigger auto-selects wave parallel when at least one wave has 2+ independent stories
Decision is logged to terminal: '[orchestration] Using sequential|wave-parallel (reason)' before story execution begins
The parallelism number input / toggle is removed from the pipeline trigger UI
A read-only badge replaces it showing auto-selected mode and wave structure
The rorca-forge-brief-first spec (FG-001 has no deps, all others depend on FG-001) auto-selects sequential
A spec with 3+ independent Wave 0 stories auto-selects wave parallel

userStories.title: Surface Wave Failure Root Cause in UI
userStories.description: When a wave run fails (0/N stories passed), the UI currently shows 'Failed/blocked: FG-001, FG-002, ...' in the terminal with no explanation of WHY FG-001 failed. The Stories tab just shows all stories as failed/skipped. Fix: (1) When a story fails in wave execution, the terminal output from that story's Claude subprocess (stdout + stderr from the sub-worktree) should be captured and surfaced. Currently sub-worktree output goes to a per-story log file — add a 'Story Log' expandable section in the Stories tab for each failed story showing the last 50 lines of its execution output. (2) Add a prominent error banner at the top of the run view when wave execution results in 0 passes: 'Run failed: FG-001 (root cause) blocked 5 downstream stories. See story log for details.' (3) In the Stories tab, visually distinguish between stories that FAILED (ran and failed) vs stories that were BLOCKED (never ran due to upstream failure) — failed stories get a red badge, blocked/skipped stories get a grey 'Blocked by FG-001' badge.
acceptanceCriteria: Failed stories in the Stories tab have a 'View Log' button showing last 50 lines of Claude subprocess output
Blocked stories show a grey 'Blocked by <story-id>' badge identifying which upstream story caused the block
When 0/N stories pass in a wave run, a prominent error banner identifies the root cause story
The error banner text: 'FG-001 failed and blocked N downstream stories. View story log →'
Failed vs blocked stories are visually distinct (red badge vs grey badge) in the Stories tab
Story log is captured from sub-worktree execution output and stored in story_results.log_path

userStories.title: Fix Terminal Streaming — execution-engine.ts Stdout Forwarding
userStories.description: execution-engine.ts writes Claude subprocess stdout to a log file (e.g. forge/specs/logs/FG-001_<timestamp>.log) for persistence, but does NOT also forward it to execution-engine's own stdout. The backend captures execution-engine's stdout into an in-memory buffer (keyed by runId) and streams it to the frontend terminal via SSE at GET /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/output. Because execution-engine.ts never writes Claude output to its own stdout, the buffer is empty and the terminal is permanently blank for all runs using the new engine. The old run-loop.ts piped Claude stdout directly through to its own stdout, which the backend captured naturally. Fix: in execution-engine.ts, when spawning the Claude subprocess, use a tee-like pattern — write each chunk of Claude stdout to BOTH the log file AND process.stdout. This restores terminal streaming without removing log file persistence. Specifically: use child_process.spawn with stdio pipe, attach a data listener on child.stdout that (a) appends to the log file write stream and (b) calls process.stdout.write(chunk). Same pattern for stderr. This is the same contract run-loop.ts fulfilled and that the backend's output buffer expects.
acceptanceCriteria: Terminal tab shows live Claude output (tool calls, text, results) during a run using execution-engine.ts
Semantic log view parses execution-engine.ts output the same way it parsed run-loop.ts output
Log file (forge/specs/logs/<storyId>_<timestamp>.log) is still written with complete output
Both stdout AND stderr from Claude subprocess are forwarded to process.stdout (and therefore the SSE buffer)
A run started after this fix shows output in the terminal within 30 seconds of FG-001 starting
Late-joining viewers (opening terminal tab after run started) receive buffered replay from process start
